support_spans: CT chest/abdomen: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia
contradict_spans: Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels
concepts.why: The presence of cavitary lesions in the lungs suggests pneumococcal infection, but the gram-positive cocci in vessels are more indicative of Staphylococcal sepsis.

support_spans: Purpuric retiform patches on each flank
contradict_spans: Tissue Gram staining: Gram-positive cocci in vessels
concepts.why: The presence of purpuric retiform patches is suggestive of meningococcal sepsis, but the gram-positive cocci in vessels are not typical of this infection.

support_spans: diffuse papules on the trunk and extremities
Hyponatremia and neutropenia present
concepts.why: The presence of diffuse papules, hyponatremia, and neutropenia are consistent with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome, but the gram-positive cocci in vessels are more indicative of Staphylococcal sepsis.

rationales.F06: Purpuric retiform patches are suggestive of a severe bacterial infection, which could be consistent with Staphylococcal or Meningococcal sepsis.
rationales.F10: Cavitary lesions in lungs representing necrotizing pneumonia are highly suggestive of a severe bacterial infection, which could be consistent with Staphylococcal sepsis.
rationales.F11: Small organisms within vasculature found in punch biopsy are highly suggestive of a bacterial infection, which could be consistent with Staphylococcal or Meningococcal sepsis.
rationales.F12: Gram-positive cocci in vessels found in tissue Gram staining are highly suggestive of Staphylococcal sepsis, and rule out Meningococcal and Pneumococcal sepsis.
